expectedEnglishScientificConditions.expectation: Frictional electrification involves charged-particle transfer, commonly electrons. An electron carries one negative elementary charge. Do not assert that all charged particles carry one positive elementary charge.
expectedEnglishScientificConditions.boundary: Choose the rubbed bodies and relevant charged particles together; no charge crosses this whole-system boundary. Its signed total charge stays fixed.
expectedEnglishScientificConditions.initialValue: A zero algebraic sum after electrification follows only if the total was initially zero. Individual bodies may gain or lose electrons.

expectedEnglishScientificConditions.expectation: Charge-isolated explicitly means no electric charge crosses the chosen boundary. The algebraic sum of all particle charges stays constant at its initial value, which can be nonzero.
expectedEnglishScientificConditions.distinctions: Internal charge transfer is allowed. Particle-number constancy is not required. Whether energy is exchanged is a separate condition.

expectedEnglishScientificConditions.expectation: Preserve the q-sum equation's original mathematical atoms and label (8-1), translating only the constant's language. Terms are signed charges; the constant is initial total charge, not necessarily zero. Do not sum only absolute magnitudes.
expectedEnglishScientificConditions.nativeMathGate: Already executed by author; do not rerun.

expectedEnglishScientificConditions.expectation: Charge conservation is not charged-particle-number conservation. Particle production, transformation and loss of original particle identity are allowed while total charge is conserved for a complete charge-isolated process.
expectedEnglishScientificConditions.examplesNotUniversalRestrictions: Equal-magnitude opposite-sign pair creation or pair annihilation are examples, not a claim that every particle process is pair-only or that each product must be neutral.
expectedEnglishScientificConditions.footnoteAnchor: Preserve the original particle-production/transformation footnote reference.

expectedEnglishScientificConditions.expectation: Preserve the original tenth-grade-textbook footnote about particle production and interconversion, explicitly attributed to the original book rather than presented as today's learner navigation.

Experiments support charge conservation as a basic charge property. The book's claim that its cause was unknown must be explicitly historical and not a complete contemporary conclusion. Deeper theory is outside this lesson; retain signed-total-charge bookkeeping as the present learning focus.
